question: Does search breadth alone explain the 2mm loss? Guard FIXED at the shipped 0.010; only POLICY_ATTEMPT_BUDGET varies. Six scenario-matrix scenes, policy_timeout 20, 2 workers, this container.
answer: NO -- and it REFUTES the "more candidates make this ranker worse" generalisation written in the previous commit. At a fixed guard, more search is monotonically BETTER on both placed and physical survival: attempts/step 1739/2558/3411 give placed 110/164/172 and physical deaths 2/4/1, against the shipped deadline point (3651 attempts/step, placed 183, 0 physical deaths on these scenes). The pi_B ladder therefore measured a STARVED operating point (~2500 attempts/step, ~30% below shipped) where both guard arms lose episodes to physical settle failures for a reason unrelated to the guard, which is why it could not rank them. Both arms consumed the same work there (10mm 2496, 2mm 2495 attempts/step), so the ladder was a fair comparison of the wrong regime.
guard_effect_is_direct: Under the shipped deadline 2mm reaches MORE attempts (4518 vs 3651) and MORE accepted candidates (850 vs 565) than 10mm and still loses, so the guard does not act through search quantity. It acts on which placements are legal: at 18mm total clearance the permitted placements do not survive PyBullet settle (10mm 3 completed / 0 physical, 2mm 0 completed / 4 physical on the same six scenes).
